review: Astra Ultra implemented local-edge ordinal window
findings: The FOR query uses the entire unfiltered jsonb_each(edges) stream. The exact deleted=false FILTER and C-ordered ROWS frame ending one PRECEDING count precisely the original keys strictly less than the current key. JSONB object keys are unique and nonnull; the empty preceding frame counts zero.

No lifecycle partition or deleted-row prefilter was introduced. Existing deleted=true and lifecycle skips remain inside the loop, preserving shared ordinals across both lifecycles and existing behavior for missing, JSON-null or non-boolean deletion flags.

Explicit C output ordering remains. Endpoint resolution and 55000 checks are unchanged and precede ordinal assignment. The bigint count is assigned to the existing int local at the old count-assignment location; no eager int conversion changes endpoint-error order.

Replacing SELECT INTO with assignment no longer updates the function-local FOUND at that point, but this helper contains no FOUND read. Neither its return expression nor caller-visible state depends on that local flag.

Author and generated files each equal baseline plus exactly the reviewed two replacements. Manifest changes only the matching owned.sql digest. Signatures, volatility/security/search_path, grants, 220-routine inventory, capacity/deadlines and all other graph checks are unchanged.

nativeEvidence.scope: Parent plans existing owned/edge workflows, unchanged full matrix and capacity; no native tests run by reviewer.

limitations: The source eliminates a whole-map prefix SELECT for each retained edge. This is not a measured speedup or complete graph complexity claim.
